title: Bidirectional Dijkstra in Prague: Find Routes Faster!
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra race from both the start and goal on a street-graph of Prague (Žižkov). The visualization shows how splitting the search can drastically reduce explored nodes while still guaranteeing the optimal path.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ **Bidirectional Dijkstra** powering route-finding in Prague (Žižkov)! 

On a real-world street map, we model intersections as **graph vertices** and streets as **weighted edges** (distance/time). Bidirectional Dijkstra runs two synchronized Dijkstra searches: one forward from the start and one backward from the goal, meeting near the optimal corridor. 

🔍 **Deep intuition (graph theory):** instead of expanding outward from only one source, we effectively shrink the search frontier by balancing the “wavefronts” from both ends. When the two explorations meet, the algorithm combines path costs to yield the **globally shortest path**—a classic strategy to improve efficiency while preserving correctness under nonnegative weights. 

📍 In the reel, notice how fewer nodes get explored compared to single-source search on dense urban grids.
